preconditions.description: The height h is an integer between 2 and 10^5 inclusive.
The sequence a contains exactly h + 1 integers.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, int) and 1 <= x <= 200000 for x in a)
preconditions.description: Each element a_i is an integer between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.
The sum of all elements in the sequence does not exceed 200,000.
The sequence starts with 1, representing the single root vertex.

postconditions.description: If there is only one non-isomorphic tree matching the sequence, the output is exactly 'perfect'.
If multiple non-isomorphic trees exist, the first line is 'ambiguous' and exactly two subsequent lines describe the trees.

postconditions.expression: (not is_perfect) and all(isinstance(int(x), int) for x in output_lines[1].split()) and all(isinstance(int(x), int) for x in output_lines[2].split())
postconditions.description: The two tree descriptions consist of space-separated integers representing parent indices.

postconditions.expression: (not is_perfect) and len(output_lines[1].split()) == sum(a) and len(output_lines[2].split()) == sum(a)
postconditions.description: Each tree description contains exactly sum(a) integers, one for each vertex.

postconditions.expression: (not is_perfect) and (0 in tree1_parents) and (0 in tree2_parents) and tree1_parents.count(0) == 1 and tree2_parents.count(0) == 1
postconditions.description: Each tree description has exactly one root (parent 0).

postconditions.expression: (not is_perfect) and all(0 <= p < total_vertices for p in tree1_parents) and all(0 <= p < total_vertices for p in tree2_parents)
postconditions.description: All parent indices in both trees are valid vertex indices within the range [0, total_vertices - 1].

postconditions.expression: (not is_perfect) and is_valid_tree(tree1_parents, a) and is_valid_tree(tree2_parents, a)
postconditions.description: Both constructed trees match the given sequence a (i.e., the number of vertices at each distance from the root matches a_i).
The two constructed trees are non-isomorphic.
